newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Oct electricity end up, erasing early losses - SEP 09.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Oct electricity end up, erasing early losses - SEP 09.

text.p: NYMEX October electricity futures ended up Monday, erasing earlier losses tied to softer spot prices in the West amid mild weather and lower Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) prices, traders and brokers said.
A late round of buying pushed the October contracts into positive territory, industry sources said.

Earlier today, the futures and cash markets took a cue from BPA's price decrease for daily power. The discount indicated there was still an ample amount of hydropower produced in the Northwest despite scaled back operations at most hydroelectric projects after the fish migration season, they said.
"They (BPA) do have plenty power offered on peak, off peak and rest of the week," said one New York-based broker.
"There's pretty low demand in the Northwest," a Houston trader said, adding prices in the Southwest remained supported by steady cooling demand and firm natural gas prices.
October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up two cents at $16.22 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $15.95 and $16.40.
November COB finished down 15 cents at $16.60. Other active COB months ended mixed.
October Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up seven cents at $16.60 after moving in a narrow 10 cent range.
November PV finished flat against Friday's settlement of $15.40. Most active deferred PV contracts ended lower.
Until there were fresh fundamentals, the complex would continue to trade in its recent range.
"We seemed to be locked in a range," said the Houston trader.
NYMEX estimated 118 COB and 93 PV contracts were sold.
